memoryText: For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Romans 3:23-24 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
These two verses hold the whole gospel in a few lines. They tell the problem and the solution.

“For all have sinned.” The word “all” leaves no exceptions. The Jew with the law and the Gentile without it, the moral and the immoral, the religious and the irreligious. No one is left out.

“And fall short of the glory of God.” Sin is not only breaking rules. It is falling short of the purpose for which we were made: to reflect God’s glory. We were made to image him, and we have failed.

“And are justified.” Here is the turn. The word is a legal one: declared righteous, acquitted, accepted. This is God’s verdict over those who believe.

“By his grace as a gift.” Not by merit or effort, but freely. A gift cannot be earned, only received. Grace means undeserved favor, and the word “gift” underlines it.

“Through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.” Redemption means buying back, as a slave is ransomed. The price was the blood of Christ. All of this is “in Christ Jesus.” Outside of him there is no justification; in him there is no condemnation.

If you are tempted to think you are too bad to be forgiven, or good enough not to need it, say these verses. They fit both temptations.
weekInReview: This week you saw Paul’s verdict and the gospel that answers it. In Romans 3, every mouth was stopped: no one is righteous, and the law brings knowledge of sin. Then came the great “But now”: the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, and we are justified by grace as a gift, through the redemption in Christ Jesus, whom God put forward as a propitiation by his blood. In a doctrinal pause, you studied justification by faith alone: God declares sinners righteous because Christ’s righteousness is counted as theirs. Romans 4 used Abraham, who believed God and was counted righteous before circumcision and long before the law. Three psalms of repentance gave the heart’s side: Psalm 32, the blessing of the one whose sin is not counted; Psalm 130, with the LORD there is plentiful redemption; and Psalm 143, enter not into judgment with your servant.
reflectionQuestions: Which do you find harder to believe: that you are a sinner who cannot save yourself, or that you are fully forgiven and accepted in Christ? Why?
Paul says Jesus was put forward as a propitiation so that God could be both just and the justifier of the one who has faith. How does the cross show both God’s justice and God’s love at once?
David hid his sin and his bones wasted away, and then he confessed and was forgiven. Is there a sin you have been carrying in silence? What would it look like to confess it this week?
prayerPrompts: Thank God that you are justified by grace as a gift.
Rest in the work that Christ finished.
Tell him that you are not earning it.
